# Autoware 3×3 with the executor pool pinned to the allowed CPUs (2026-09-08) — Generated by Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic)

Follow-up to `notes/executor_threads_vs_cpuset.md`: repeat the split-CPU Autoware
campaign with `FISH_NPROC=6` so that `MultiThreadedExecutor` sizes its pool from
the CPUs the application actually gets, and see how much of the measured overhead
was scheduling contention rather than instrumentation cost.

## What ran

    scripts/autoware_runs/run_overhead_modes_nproc.sh          # copy of run_overhead_modes.sh
    FISH_APP_CPUS=0,2,4,6,8,10  FISH_OBS_CPUS=12-17  FISH_NPROC=6
    IMG=autoware-dev-trt-a1000-fishwait10:latest  REPS=3  RATE=0.5
    MODES="baseline lttng nsys"

* campaign dir `~/fish_traces/overhead_aw_20260908_042027_np6/`, log
  `~/fish_traces/campaign_np6_20260908_042027.log`
* 9/9 runs completed, all `exec rc=0`, 220–225 nodes stable in every run
* sessions: lttng `fish_20260908_022914 / _024207 / _025539`,
  nsys `fish_20260908_030855 / _031937 / _033007`
* host: `host_perf_mode.sh split` (SMT off, turbo off, performance governor,
  P-cores 0,2,4,6,8,10 for the app, E-cores 12-17 for the observer, 18-19 desktop)
* reference campaign (same host mode, same image, **no** shim):
  `~/fish_traces/overhead_aw_20260906_163330`

The shim is `scripts/fish_nproc/libfish_nproc.so`, bind-mounted read-only into the
container and `LD_PRELOAD`ed **only** on the application command
(`env LD_PRELOAD=… FISH_NPROC=6 taskset -c $FISH_APP_CPUS ros2 launch …`); the
observer side (LTTng daemons, FISH daemon, probes) runs unmodified.

## The shim does what it claims

Control experiment in a fresh container, pinned to the desktop cores so the
campaign was not disturbed — a bare `component_container_mt`, nothing loaded:

| setting | threads in the process |
|---|--:|
| plain | **24** (pool = 14 = online CPUs) |
| `FISH_NPROC=6` | **16** (pool = 6) |
| `FISH_NPROC=2` | 12 (pool = 2) |

In the campaign itself, `component_container_mt` processes from the session
snapshots (`snapshot/ps_tree.txt`):

| campaign | threads per container (max … median) |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-06, no shim | 51, 45, 35, 34, 34, 33 … **median 33** |
| 2026-09-08, `FISH_NPROC=6` | 43, 37, 27, 26, 26, 25 … **median 25** |

−8 threads per container, exactly the 14→6 pool change; node count identical
(225), so the system under measurement is otherwise the same.

## Result — the overhead is unchanged

Same protocol, same metrics (Autoware's own `/diagnostics`), 3 reps per mode.

| metric | mode | pool = 6 (2026-09-08) | pool = 14 (2026-09-06) | Δ |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CPU cores (busiest 60 s) | baseline | 2.88±0.04 | 2.91±0.02 | −0.8 % |
| | lttng | 5.15±0.16 | 5.10±0.04 | +0.9 % |
| | nsys | 5.06±0.06 | 5.23±0.09 | −3.3 % |
| app-set cores | baseline | 2.59±0.02 | 2.58±0.00 | +0.3 % |
| | lttng | 4.50±0.13 | 4.43±0.05 | +1.6 % |
| | nsys | 4.42±0.12 | 4.61±0.07 | −4.1 % |
| observer-set cores | baseline | 0.35±0.03 | 0.34±0.00 | +2.7 % |
| | lttng | 2.48±0.14 | 2.50±0.04 | −0.7 % |
| | nsys | 2.26±0.13 | 2.43±0.13 | −6.8 % |
| concat processing [ms] | baseline | 8.12±0.08 | 8.25±0.07 | −1.6 % |
| | lttng | 10.57±0.07 | 10.61±0.20 | −0.4 % |
| | nsys | 10.41±0.35 | 10.69±0.48 | −2.5 % |
| centerpoint proc [ms] | baseline | 23.21±0.27 | 23.54±0.10 | −1.4 % |
| | lttng | 23.39±0.59 | 23.27±0.30 | +0.5 % |
| | nsys | 24.22±0.82 | 24.19±0.57 | +0.1 % |
| Total Latency [ms] | baseline | 401.87±7.10 | 402.39±4.56 | −0.1 % |
| | lttng | 433.03±14.63 | 430.63±10.76 | +0.6 % |
| | nsys | 430.45±2.56 | 428.21±13.56 | +0.5 % |
| objects rate [Hz] | baseline | 9.79±0.06 | 9.77±0.06 | +0.2 % |
| | lttng | 9.74±0.10 | 9.92±0.13 | −1.8 % |
| | nsys | 9.83±0.10 | 9.79±0.06 | +0.4 % |
| warm-up [sim s] | nsys | 5.99±0.19 | 7.17±0.84 | −16.4 % |

Tracing overhead as reported by each campaign on its own baseline:

| | pool = 6 | pool = 14 |
|---|--:|--:|
| CPU, lttng | +78.6 % | +75.5 % |
| CPU, nsys | +75.6 % | +80.1 % |
| concat processing, lttng | +30.1 % | +28.5 % |
| concat processing, nsys | +28.2 % | +29.5 % |
| Total Latency, lttng | +7.8 % | +7.0 % |
| Total Latency, nsys | +7.1 % | +6.4 % |

**Reading:** every difference between the two campaigns is inside the run-to-run
spread of three repetitions; nothing moves systematically. Sizing the executor
pool to the CPUs the application is allowed to use changes neither the baseline
nor the measured tracing overhead on this workload. The only visible (still
noisy) effect is a shorter warm-up in the nsys mode (7.2 → 6.0 sim s), which is
where thread startup would show up if anywhere.

**Consequence for the paper:** the overhead numbers of the 2026-09-06 campaign
stand as they are; the 20-vs-6 thread question does not need a caveat beyond one
sentence stating that the pool is sized from the visible topology and that
pinning it changes nothing measurable. The 2026-09-08 campaign is the evidence
for that sentence.

## Concurrency profile — the contention is gone

Time-weighted distribution of callbacks that are started-but-not-finished,
computed from `ros2:callback_start/end` paired per thread (session ingested into
PG; the same method for both campaigns):

nsys mode, like for like (`fish_20260906_151532` vs `fish_20260908_030855`):

| | pool = 14 | pool = 6 |
|---|--:|--:|
| callback executions in the trace | 1 390 238 | 706 035 |
| **max callbacks in flight** | **21** | **11** |
| **time with more in flight than CPUs (>6)** | **5.01 %** | **0.07 %** |
| time with >12 in flight | 0.12 % | 0.00 % |
| idle (nothing executing) | 74.96 % | 72.91 % |

The lttng-mode session of the same campaign (`fish_20260908_022914`) gives the
same picture: 697 337 executions, max 12 in flight, >6 for 0.10 % of the time.

So the mechanism the shim targets did what it was supposed to: with the pool
sized to the allowance, the run essentially never has more callbacks in flight
than CPUs (5.01 % → 0.10 % of wall time), and the peak drops from 21 to 12.
**And the end-to-end metrics did not move** — which is the answer to the
question this campaign was run for: the contention was real but not what the
overhead numbers were made of.

## Unexpected: the traced system does half the internal work

Every np6 trace is half the size of its 2026-09-06 counterpart (111 vs 222 MB
CTF, in all six traced runs), with 0 discarded events on both sides and the same
tracepoint set (`extra_events.txt` is identical, `rmw_take` filtered on
`taken == 1`).  Inside the identical 153–154 s launch→replay-end window:

| | pool = 14 | pool = 6 |
|---|--:|--:|
| callback executions per second | 8 974 | 4 539 |
| `rcl_publish` per second | 547 | 270 |
| traced processes / threads | 90 / 696 | 74 / 506 |

The reduction is *uniform across every process* (e.g. `component_container_mt`
processes together: 2.70 M → 1.36 M events, 20 processes on both sides) and is
dominated by the two `rclcpp::TimeSource` callbacks — the per-node `/clock`
subscriptions — plus `/diagnostics` and `/parameter_events`.  Application-level
behaviour is unchanged: objects 9.8 Hz, obstacle pointcloud ~9 Hz, CenterPoint
23 ms, Total Latency ~430 ms in both.

Most likely reading: with 6 executor threads the containers no longer keep up
with the 225-node `/clock` fan-out under tracing load, and the middleware drops
clock messages (small queue) instead of queueing them — the callbacks simply do
not fire.  Nothing in the perception chain depends on that resolution, so the
end-to-end numbers stay put.

**This is a caveat, not a bug in the measurement**: the two campaigns are not the
same system internally.  Before the shim is used for anything but this
experiment, the `/clock` delivery rate per node should be measured explicitly
(count `TimeSource::create_clock_sub` executions per node per second, and check
`/clock` publish vs receive counts) to confirm the drop and decide whether it is
acceptable.

* script (new, original untouched): `scripts/autoware_runs/run_overhead_modes_nproc.sh`
* shim + probe: `scripts/fish_nproc/`

  `FISH_NPROC_LIB=…`); note that `<run>/cpuset.txt` does **not** carry it — the
  script writes that file with `>` right after the shim lines, so they are
